chapters.summary: Micah declares God's judgment on Samaria and Jerusalem because of their sin, and calls the people to mourn and repent.
keyPoints: The LORD comes down from his holy temple to judge all peoples, bearing witness against Israel's rebellion.
Samaria and Jerusalem are punished for idolatry and deceit, and are reduced to ruins.
The prophet weeps and urges the people to repent as disaster draws near, yet judgment is certain to come.
chapters.application: When we wander from God in our own lives, let us heed his warnings and turn back to him without delay, so that we do not forfeit his blessing.

chapters.summary: Micah condemns the evil deeds of Israel's leaders and declares God's judgment, yet promises that a remnant will return and that a shepherd will one day lead them.
keyPoints: Leaders plot evil, oppress the people, and seize their inheritance - so God will surely bring disaster.
False prophets mislead the people with promises of peace, but the word of the LORD will surely come to pass.
God promises that the remnant will return like sheep to the fold, freed from the grip of their enemies.
chapters.application: Let us examine our own conduct, turn away from oppression and injustice, and in times of hardship look to God's mercy, trusting that he will lead us back to rest.

chapters.summary: Micah rebukes the injustice and deceit of the leaders and false prophets, declares that God will surely judge them, and prophesies that Zion will be punished for its sin.
keyPoints: The leaders hate what is good and pervert justice, oppressing the people as though devouring their flesh.
False prophets prophesy for money yet falsely proclaim peace, deceiving God's chosen people.
The prophet Micah, relying on the power of God, declares judgment - Zion will surely be destroyed.
chapters.application: Let us examine whether we profit through injustice or tolerate wrongdoing. May we hold fast to integrity and depend on God, never straying from justice for the sake of selfish gain.

chapters.summary: Micah 4 depicts the glory of God's kingdom in the last days, when Jerusalem becomes the center to which all nations turn, and also foretells Israel's exile and the promise of restoration.
keyPoints: In the last days, all nations will stream to the holy mountain, and the peaceful reign of God's kingdom will be revealed.
God will gather the lame and the scattered, and reestablish the remnant as a strong nation.
Though Zion suffers like a woman in labor, she will at last be redeemed and given victory.
chapters.application: In times of turmoil, let us hold fast to faith, trust that God governs history, walk humbly in his ways, and wait for the peace and restoration he has promised.

chapters.summary: Micah 5 prophesies that a ruler from Bethlehem will bring peace, and promises that the remnant of Israel will triumph through God's mighty power.
keyPoints: It is prophesied that the Messiah will come forth from Bethlehem, whose origins are from of old, from everlasting.
This ruler will shepherd his flock in the strength of the LORD, bringing peace.
The remnant, like dew and showers, will depend on God to overcome their enemies and bring about peace.
chapters.application: In times of turmoil, let us look to the Savior who comes from Bethlehem, who gives peace and guidance; may we trust his promises and live out peace and hope.

chapters.summary: Through the prophet Micah, God lays out his case against Israel, showing that although they observe religious rituals, they lack justice and mercy - true worship consists in doing justice, loving mercy, and walking with God.
keyPoints: God calls the mountains and the ends of the earth to hear his case, reminding Israel that he once saved them out of Egypt.
God shows that the people's sacrifices and religious rituals cannot replace the pursuit of justice and mercy.
The prophet sums up what God requires: to do justice, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with God.
chapters.application: In daily life, let us demonstrate justice through our actions, show mercy with love, and walk humbly with God at all times - this is the worship that pleases him.

chapters.summary: Micah laments the corruption of society, yet declares God's forgiveness and faithfulness, closing the book with praise and hope.
keyPoints: The prophet laments that the godly have vanished, and society is filled with oppression and injustice.
He warns that people's hearts are deceitful, so that even friends and family cannot be trusted.
He looks to God, who forgives iniquity because he keeps covenant and shows steadfast love.
chapters.application: Even when our surroundings are dark, let us hold fast to faith, for God's mercy is abundant; he will surely forgive our sins and guide us to walk in the light.
